items.text: REFERRED TO CIVIL SERVICE AND PENSIONS

items.actClause: AN ACT to amend the retirement and social security law, in relation to disability benefits for certain members of the New York city fire department pension fund or the New York city employees' retirement system
items.memo:
BILL NUMBER:  S7105

 TITLE OF BILL :

An act to amend the retirement and social security law, in relation to
disability benefits for certain members of the New York city fire
department pension fund or the New York city employees' retirement
system

 SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS :

This legislation would amend the New York State Retirement and Social
Security Law to change the calculation of Ordinary Disability
Retirement (ODR) and Accident Disability Retirement (ADR) benefits for
Tier 3 and Tier 6 members of the Fire Department Pension Fund and
uniformed members of the Department of Correction in the New York City
Employees' Retirement System.  Specifically, this legislation:

*Provides an accident disability benefit equal to three-quarters of
Final Average Salary (FAS)
*Defines FAS as an average of wages earned over a five-year period
*Excludes certain lump sum payments from the definition of wages
*Includes presumptive disability provisions for certain diseases
*Removes the Social Security Offset from disability benefits
*Includes Tier 2 Cost-of-Living Adjustment provisions
*Requires that eligible members contribute an additional three percent
of wages

 REASONS FOR SUPPORT :

The City of New York deeply appreciates the service of its uniformed
employees. Our City's heroes need strong disability protections in
light of the dangers they face on a daily basis.

The City also needs a pension system that doesn't unfairly burden
taxpayers. That is why the City worked closely with public employee
unions representing New York City Firefighters and Correction Officers
to craft this legislation, which would allow the uniformed employees
they represent to receive an accident disability pension equal to
three-quarters of FAS. This legislation represents a responsible
compromise plan that ensures that our brave uniformed men and women
would receive coverage in the event of tragic injury, while protecting
taxpayers from exorbitant pension costs. The City looks forward to
working closely with public employee unions representing other
uniformed titles to reach an agreement that would extend the same
disability protections to their employees.

This legislation modifies the disability laws put in place by New York
State in 2009 and 2012, but stops short of a complete rollback of the
Governor's pension reforms that the Legislature passed and the
Governor signed a few years ago. It recognizes that our uniformed
employees must have disability benefits which protect them and their
families in the event of injury while performing their job duties. The
bill also recognizes the increasing costs of public employee pensions,
currently over $9 billion annually in the non-discretionary portion of
the City's budget, which has an impact on the City's ability to
deliver vital services to its residents. This common sense compromise
plan agreed upon by the City and public employee unions honors our
heroes while preserving fiscal responsibility for New York City and,
therefore, should be adopted by the Legislature.

 FISCAL IMPACT :

See fiscal note

 EFFECTIVE DATE :
This act shall take effect immediately

summary: Relates to disability benefits for NYC fire department members who are New York city enhanced plan members.
